name: Customer Ease Lens
philosophy: The customer does not care about your architecture. They care about whether they can understand, trust, and finish what they came to do. Friction is failure. Every extra click, term, decision, or delay is a request to go away. Measure success by the customer's first completed value moment.
evidence: Every abandoned onboarding flow traced to a single unexplained question or surprise delay.
Products that reduced first-use friction outperformed feature-rich competitors in adoption.
strengths: Testing language from the user's perspective
blind_spots: May push for oversimplified flows that hide necessary complexity
Can ignore backend reliability if the front end feels smooth
May prioritize new users over power users

disagreement_profile.typical_conflict: Customer ease may demand more options; Jobs demands fewer.
Friction removal can be expensive with indirect return.
